cards.title: Accops HySecure ZTNA Product Presentation: Zero Trust Private Access, QRNG, Editions and the Forcepoint SSE Joint Solution (2026)
cards.client: Five named reference customers used as case-study slides: a Kuwaiti airline, a Middle East retail group with 20,000+ employees, an Indian government e-governance agency running 600+ applications for 500,000+ users, India's largest e-commerce company, and an Indian broking/financial-services firm - plus one unnamed 'customer of national interest' for the post-quantum story. A reference-customer logo wall covers banks, financial services, education, healthcare, pharma, government and manufacturing.
cards.client_actual: Case-study slides: Jazeera Airlines (Aviation / Kuwait), Apparel Group (Retail / UAE), NIC - National Informatics Centre (Government / India / North), Flipkart (E-Commerce / India / South), Kotak Securities (FSI / India / West), plus 'Confidential Customer - a customer of national interest' (Government / India) on the QRNG slide. Technology partners named: Nutanix, Microsoft, Supermicro, RedHat, HPE, Dell, VMware (Broadcom), Proxmox. Tested SSE co-existence: Zscaler, Palo Alto, Netskope. Logo wall slides are images and carry no extractable names.
cards.key_problem: An organisation still on a firewall/VPN perimeter treats its internal network as trusted: there is little user or device validation, every firewall port is reachable once a user is on, lateral movement is open, and a single compromised desktop becomes the weakest link - while the business needs app-level access for employees, BYOD users, vendors, dealers and call-centre agents.
key_outcomes: The core ZTNA pitch in three stages (authenticate, segment the network, segment the applications): one gateway as the single point of entry, per-app validation, users see only the ports allowed for that user and device, applications hidden from internet users, continuous trust evaluation

Two deployment stories side by side: HySecure as a virtual appliance 100% on-premises or on cloud with an App Connector, and 'ZTNA as a Service' via the Accops ZTNA Cloud with outbound-only tunnels, built-in DDoS/WAF, included load balancer, logs and telemetry held in a sovereign cloud, DC-DR built in and 99.99% uptime

Twelve-point solution summary: 100% on-premises, CARTA contextual access, multi-protocol (web, TCP, UDP, VoIP), reverse connect with no inbound ports, web application protection, built-in DLP, IdP integration, high-capacity scale, N+1 high availability, micro-segmentation, advanced reporting and CERT-In audit validation

Web Application Protection detail: OWASP Top 10, WASEC 50, 4000+ built-in signatures, AI/ML zero-day model, custom positive/negative rules, virtual patching, anti-bot (device fingerprinting, AI bot detection, Captcha, crypto challenge), API protection including hidden and stale API discovery, built-in AV scanning and sandboxing, privacy enforcement with data masking

Posture check across device identity (domain/certificate/hardware ID), device health (AV/EDR status, OS and browser version, custom file/registry/process rules), user role, access pattern, time and location, assessed continuously

On-demand DLP menu: restrict data copy, block screen-scraping and screen-sharing tools, download blocking, view-only access, on-demand file encryption, keylogger protection, watermarking, internet whitelisting without a web proxy, browser isolation, convert PC to kiosk, Bluetooth and USB restriction

Post-quantum section: Kyber768 and Kyber1024 support, envelope encryption of API data inside TLS, and integration with Made-in-India QRNG appliances for random seed generation on both gateway and agent

Eight generic use cases (legacy VPN replacement, secure BYOD, read-only/kiosk alternative to VDI, agentless web-app access, L3 access for mobile developers, micro-branch connectivity, last-mile MPLS failover, PQC enablement without app changes) plus four vertical ones for FSI, Manufacturing, IT/ITeS and Retail

Four HySecure editions (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum) broken out by access mode, posture check, MFA/SSO, endpoint controls and reporting, with add-ons priced separately; licensing is named-user or concurrent-user, perpetual or subscription

An explicit 'what we do not do' slide: HySecure is not an SSE solution - no SWG/web proxy for internet apps, no endpoint DLP, no network DLP, domain-level whitelist/blacklist only, copy protection is all-or-nothing rather than data-classification driven

Accops + Forcepoint joint solution: Accops supplies ZTNA, IAM/MFA/SSO, virtual apps and desktops and thin OS, Forcepoint supplies SWG, CASB, DLP and DSPM, with two capability tables comparing the pair against 'Competition' and a 'why this wins' close (on-prem/hybrid/sovereign, identity++, validated integration, value for money, integrated support)
cards.brief: A 38-slide HySecure product presentation from the Webinars folder, copyright 2026. It opens with the Zero Trust model and a three-stage framing, gives a short About Us and What We Do, then contrasts a current VPN/VLAN setup against ZTNA before introducing HySecure in two architectures (on-premises policy enforcer plus app connector, and ZTNA-as-a-Service over outbound tunnels). The middle is feature depth - web application protection, posture check, on-demand DLP - followed by use cases, five customer case studies in problem/challenge/need/solution/benefits format, a post-quantum block built on a published RSA quantum-attack paper plus the QRNG integration and a confidential government win, then editions, licensing, 'why Accops', an honest limitations slide, how HySecure co-exists with SSE, a competitive slide against ZPA/NPA/Prisma, and a closing Forcepoint partnership section with two capability tables. Note that 'RBI' appears on two slides meaning two different things: on slide 30 and in one slide 32 bullet it is Remote Browser Isolation, while another slide 32 bullet refers to the Reserve Bank of India's auto-deactivation requirement. The architecture slides are largely diagram text, so read the original deck before quoting a flow.
cards.use_for: The current end-to-end HySecure ZTNA presentation - use it for a webinar, a first product session, or any prospect replacing a legacy VPN. Strongest for: VPN replacement, BYOD and vendor/third-party access with on-demand DLP, agentless access to private web apps, post-quantum/QRNG conversations, and any deal where on-premises deployment or data sovereignty beats a cloud-only ZTNA. Slide 30 ('what we do not do') and slide 31-32 are the ones to read before an SSE conversation - they say plainly where HySecure stops and how it co-exists with or differs from Zscaler, Palo Alto and Netskope. Slides 33-38 are the Accops + Forcepoint joint pitch when a customer wants SSE and ZTNA together. Internal reference: trim the customer-specific and limitations slides before sending anything to a prospect.
cards.stale_risk: The deck contradicts itself on the Gartner claim: the About Us slide still says 'In 2023 & 2024 Gartner Magic Quadrant, as well as 2023 Market Guide for DaaS', while a later slide says 'Two Consecutive Years in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for DaaS 2025 | 2026'. Use the 2025|2026 claim. The Forcepoint section states 'Accops SaaS ZTNA will be available by end of year' - a roadmap promise that dates quickly and should be checked before it is repeated to a customer. The twelve-point summary slide is not generic: it names NIC IdP (Parichay/Pehchan), NIC SIEM, CERT-In audit and a '5+ lakh users, sized for 3.75 lakh at <=70% utilization' figure, all carried over from a specific government engagement. Edition contents point readers to www.accops.com for the latest, so the Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum table may already have moved on.
